_control.saw: The two control clips are the cleanest result in the sweep and they disagree with each other. Same subject, same seed, same motion prompt, same 8 seconds; the only difference is which engine drew the keyframe. The anime control's fine detail is FLAT across the whole clip (octiles 1.01 1.02 1.05 1.07 1.06 1.02 1.01 1.01) - it ends with as much fine structure as it started with. The qwen control decays monotonically from the first octile to the last (1.00 0.99 0.98 0.95 0.93 0.91 0.89 0.87), and by 8s the skin has gone slightly waxy and the background softer. Both keep the subject and both keep the shot; the qwen one pushes in slowly. This pair is the reference: any style claim about video survival has to beat its own engine's control, not the other engine's.
_control.works_for: n/a - this is a reference frame, not a style. MEASURED baseline for the video pass, from the same 8.04s LTX i2v render every style in the sweep got: the anime control holds fine detail flat across 8s (detail 1.007, boil 0.091, motion 0.423) while the qwen control decays steadily (detail 0.870, boil 0.228, motion 0.753). Read every style's video numbers against ITS OWN engine's control - the engine gap is larger than most style effects.

flat_vector.failure: content drift - background architecture rearranges, unrequested push-in
flat_vector.saw: The idiom is untouched at 8 seconds. Solid fills stay solid, the heavy black contours stay hard, the five-colour red/grey/white palette never widens. The card's named failure - edges softening and gradients creeping in - did not happen at all; at native resolution frame 192 is as crisp as frame 0. What does fail is everything except the style: the buildings continuously rearrange themselves, doors and windows slide and change shape, and the camera pushes in although the prompt pinned it. This was the highest-motion clip in the whole sweep (2.772), which is where its boil 0.302 and detail 0.866 come from - not from the style decaying.
flat_vector.works_for: video - CONFIRMED by render, and it is the strongest kind of confirmation because the failure the card predicted was looked for and is absent. Over 8.04s the flat fills, hard contours and limited palette are indistinguishable at frame 192 from frame 0; no edge softening, no gradient creep. The real risk with this style in motion is elsewhere: it produced the most movement of any style in the sweep (motion 2.772 from a prompt asking for almost none), the background geometry rearranges continuously, and the camera pushed in despite being told not to. Use it for shots where the subject carries the frame, not where background continuity has to read.

ligne_claire.failure: background line-field reorganises; highest boil in the sweep but not from the idiom
ligne_claire.saw: The line idiom holds perfectly - even outline weight, flat fills, no shading creeping in, and the face stays cleanly drawn for the full 8 seconds. It also scored the HIGHEST boil in the entire sweep (0.405), and looking at the strip tells you why the number is misleading: this style fills the background with a dense field of thin coloured architectural lines, and that field continuously reorganises. It is content churn in a high-frequency image, not the style failing. The subject and framing stay put the whole time - unlike the photographic clips at comparable motion, this one never loses its shot.
ligne_claire.works_for: video - CONFIRMED to hold, and it is the clearest demonstration in the sweep that boil does not measure style survival. The even outline weight and flat fills are intact at 8.04s and the subject stays framed throughout. But it recorded the highest boil of any style measured (0.405) purely because its dense background line-field reorganises frame to frame; detail 0.859. Prefer it where the background can be simple - a busy ligne-claire street will visibly rebuild itself behind a static subject over 8 seconds.

silhouette_poster.saw: Joint most stable clip in the sweep: boil 0.071, detail 1.001, octiles flat from end to end, motion 0.415. The heavy black masses hold their shape, the warm limited palette never shifts, and hair drift is the only movement. The card's one specific warning - that i2v invents detail inside large empty regions, so watch for a face fading up inside the black - did NOT happen; the blacks stay solid and empty for 8 seconds. One honest caveat on the test rather than the style: the keyframe this style produced on our subject is a high-contrast heavy-black illustration with a fully rendered face, not a true two-tone silhouette, so the largest empty-region case was only partly exercised.
silhouette_poster.works_for: video - CONFIRMED, the joint most stable style measured (boil 0.071, detail 1.001, octiles flat across 8.04s). The predicted failure was specifically looked for and did not occur: no detail faded up inside the black masses over 8 seconds. Caveat on the test, not the style - the keyframe rendered as a heavy-black high-contrast illustration with a rendered face rather than a true two-tone silhouette, so a genuinely large empty black region has still not been put through the pass.

cel_anime_90s.failure: none - including the grain the card expected to lose
cel_anime_90s.saw: Both halves of this style survive, which contradicts the card's split. The flat cel paint, hard shadow shapes and cyan/green retro palette hold exactly as predicted. But the baked analogue grain and video noise - the part the card said would boil away - is still plainly there in the background at frame 192, and the detail octiles are essentially flat (1.01 1.01 1.01 1.00 0.99 0.98 0.98 0.98, ending 0.976). boil 0.173 at motion 0.772. The grain reads as welded to the picture, not re-rolled each frame. This is the house idiom of the project and it came through the pass intact.
cel_anime_90s.works_for: video - CONFIRMED to hold, and the card's split prediction was WRONG in the style's favour. Both the flat cel paint AND the baked film grain survive 8.04s: detail octiles flat (1.01 -> 0.976), boil 0.173. The grain does not re-roll and does not smooth away - it stays welded to the picture. The old advice to strip grain from the prompt and add it in the grade instead is not needed for temporal reasons; keep it if you want it in the frame. Comfortably usable at 8 seconds.

manga_screentone.failure: none - the card's worst-case prediction is falsified
manga_screentone.saw: The headline result of the sweep. This card called itself the WORST case in the library and predicted the tone would crawl and shimmer across the whole frame; it is instead one of the most stable clips measured. Detail octiles are dead flat (0.99 0.98 0.98 0.97 0.97 0.98 0.97 0.98), boil 0.214 - below the no-style qwen control's 0.228 and far below the 0.385 that a plain ffmpeg crop-pan over a still scores from resampling alone. At native resolution the hatching stays hatching, the blacks stay solid, the halftone gradients persist, and the framing does not budge for 8 seconds. Honest caveat: the keyframe delivered mostly ink hatching with only limited literal benday dot, so the harshest form of the prediction was not maximally tested.
manga_screentone.works_for: video - MEASURED, and the previous 'WORST case in this set' prediction is FALSIFIED. Over 8.04s the monochrome ink idiom is fully intact: detail octiles dead flat (0.99 -> 0.977), boil 0.214, which is LOWER than the no-style qwen control (0.228) and far below the 0.385 an ffmpeg crop-pan scores on a still from resampling alone. The tone does not crawl and the framing does not drift. This is a video-capable style, not a stills-and-held-frames style. One caveat: the keyframe rendered mostly as ink hatching with limited literal benday dot, so a dense pure-dot field has still not been through the pass.

pointillism.failure: the style never rendered - engine/LoRA mismatch
pointillism.saw: This clip cannot answer the question it was chosen for. The keyframe is not pointillist - it is a soft anime illustration with mild stipple in the background and on the scarf. The card declares engine=anime while recommending the qwen LoRA illustration-qwen-image at 1.2, and the anime keyframe workflow (22_anime_kf_ipadapter.json) has no LoRA node at all, so the LoRA was never applied and the dot field never rendered. The video numbers that came back (detail 1.011, boil 0.147, motion 0.527) describe a soft anime illustration holding steady, which is true and useless. The dot-field prediction stands untested.
pointillism.works_for: video - STILL UNTESTED, and the attempt to test it exposed a bug. The card declares engine=anime while recommending a qwen LoRA (illustration-qwen-image), and workflow 22_anime_kf_ipadapter.json has no LoRA node, so the keyframe rendered as a soft anime illustration with no dot field and the video pass had nothing pointillist to preserve. The clip in samples/video is real but it does not test this style. Fix the engine/LoRA routing first, then re-run. comic_halftone and stop_motion_felt carry the identical mismatch. Note that the neighbouring dot-field prediction it was meant to corroborate - manga_screentone - was measured and FAILED to boil, so the prior behind 'a dot field is the worst case for temporal stability' is now doubtful rather than safe.

film_35mm.failure: grain dissolves, colour survives - the split is real
film_35mm.saw: The only card in the sweep whose split prediction is confirmed exactly as written. The warm/cool colour behaviour and the golden rim light hold completely for 8 seconds. The grain does not: it is clearly present in skin and background at frame 0, visibly reduced by frame 110, and by frame 192 replaced by smear. The octiles decay monotonically (1.00 0.97 0.95 0.93 0.93 0.93 0.92 0.86), detail 0.855 at 8s against 0.913 at 4s. There is also a push-in that contributes to the fall, but the visual reading is unambiguous - the grain is genuinely gone at the end while the colour is not.
film_35mm.works_for: video only halfway - CONFIRMED by render, and this card's split prediction was exactly right. Over 8.04s the colour and light behaviour survive intact while the grain dissolves: detail octiles decay monotonically (1.00 -> 0.855), and by frame 192 the grain is visibly replaced by smear. At 4s it is still largely there (detail 0.913), so short shots keep more of it. The existing advice stands and is now measured: if you want grain on a clip, add it to the FINISHED video with an ffmpeg noise filter rather than baking it into the keyframe.

ink_wash.failure: none - both halves of the predicted split held
ink_wash.saw: Joint lowest boil in the sweep (0.071, tied with silhouette_poster) at the second-lowest motion (0.364), detail 0.944. The card predicted a split - bold strokes hold, dry-brush greys boil - and neither half of that happened: the black strokes hold AND the dry-brush grey wash holds. The card's second-order risk is also refuted, and this is the more useful result: LTX was handed a frame that is largely empty white paper and it did NOT fill it in. The paper stays clean and empty for 8 seconds. The predicted diagnostic signature (high boil with detail near 1.0) never appeared; boil sat at the floor instead.
ink_wash.works_for: video - CONFIRMED to hold, and BOTH halves of the predicted split were wrong in the style's favour. Over 8.04s the bold black strokes and the dry-brush greys both survive: boil 0.071 (joint lowest measured, at the noise floor), detail 0.944. The documented second-order risk is also refuted - LTX was handed a frame that is largely empty white paper and did not invent anything to fill it; the paper stays clean for the full clip. One of the safest styles in the library for video.

watercolour.saw: Lowest motion in the sweep (0.345) and correspondingly quiet: boil 0.137, detail 0.976, octiles flat. The card predicted middling behaviour, with wash boundaries surviving but paper tooth and granulation not. The granulation is the interesting part and it is clearly still present in the red scarf at frame 192 - it did not smooth away. Wash boundaries hold as predicted. The one thing that does soften is the face: eyes close, features go a little muddy around the middle of the clip, but that is anatomy, not the medium.
watercolour.works_for: video - CONFIRMED, and it held BETTER than the card predicted. Over 8.04s the wash boundaries survive as expected and so does the granulation the card expected to lose: detail 0.976, boil 0.137, octiles flat, at the lowest motion measured in the sweep (0.345). Not middling - solid. The soft failure is anatomical rather than material: the face softens and goes slightly muddy mid-clip, so avoid tight facial close-ups over long shots.

photorealistic.failure: THE SHOT fails, not the style - the subject walks out of frame by 8s
photorealistic.saw: The most important clip in the sweep, and its failure has nothing to do with style. Skin texture, pores and facial structure hold beautifully through frame 137 - the predicted melting of faces and hands simply does not occur. Then the subject WALKS OUT OF FRAME. By frame 192 she is an out-of-focus red blur exiting stage left and the shot is an empty street. The octiles are flat and then cliff (1.00 1.01 1.01 0.97 0.97 0.94 0.89 0.52); detail is 0.510 at 8s but 0.964 at 4s. The 0.510 is measuring 'the subject left', not 'the texture dissolved'. At 4 seconds this clip is completely usable.
photorealistic.works_for: stills reliably. Video - MEASURED, and the result is the opposite of the old prediction. Faces and hands did NOT boil: skin texture and facial structure hold cleanly through ~5.7s. What fails is the SHOT - at 8.04s the subject walked out of frame entirely and the clip ends on an empty street (detail octiles 1.00 ... 0.89 0.52, a cliff in the final eighth). At 4s the same clip is clean (detail 0.964). Keep photographic shots to about 4 seconds; the ceiling here is composition stability, not texture. Also note the untested CAPABILITIES.md claim that Wan is the more faithful i2v remains unmeasured.

cinestill_night.saw: The halation claim is confirmed by looking at it. The red and orange bloomed point lights in the background bokeh keep their position, their colour and their bloom shape for the full 8 seconds - they never smear, migrate or multiply. The teal/red colour split holds and the face holds well through a mild push-in. detail 0.954, boil 0.195, motion 0.595. Caveat on the still rather than the clip: this keyframe is not very night-time, so what was actually tested is halation on a cool daylight frame.
cinestill_night.works_for: video - CONFIRMED by render. Halation is a per-light bloom and it holds exactly as predicted: over 8.04s the bloomed point lights keep position, colour and bloom shape without smearing or multiplying, and the teal/red split holds (detail 0.954, boil 0.195). Notably it held while film_35mm's grain did not, in the same sweep - which is the cleanest evidence in the set that the fragile thing is FINE TEXTURE, not photographic realism. Caveat: the keyframe rendered as cool daylight rather than night, so halation was tested on a daylight frame.

brutalist.failure: architecture holds rock-steady; the subject walks past camera and the shot dies
brutalist.saw: Two results in one clip. The card's actual claim - large static forms are the most stable case there is - is confirmed without reservation: the concrete slab and brick wall hold rock-steady in position and texture through frame 165, with no morphing or creep. But the same failure as photorealistic then destroys the shot: the subject walks toward and past camera, and by frame 192 the frame is out-of-focus motion. The octiles ramp down from the fourth eighth (1.00 1.00 1.00 0.95 0.89 0.80 0.66 0.45) to detail 0.442, the largest fall in the sweep, while detail at 4s is a healthy 0.934.
brutalist.works_for: video - the architecture claim is CONFIRMED and the shot-level claim is not. Over 8.04s large static forms (concrete, brick) hold rock-steady in position and texture with no morphing. But this rendered photographically, and it took the same failure as photorealistic: the subject walked past camera and by 8s the frame is out-of-focus motion (detail 0.442, the largest fall measured; octiles ramp down from the 4s mark). At 4s the clip is clean (detail 0.934). Stable for architecture; keep the shot to ~4s if a person is in it.

pixel_art.failure: the LOOK survives; the GRID loses coherence - far slower than predicted
pixel_art.saw: The card predicted the grid would shimmer apart within a second. At whole-frame scale the clip is unmistakably still pixel art at 8 seconds - chunky quantised blocks, hard aliased stair-stepping, the limited teal/red palette all intact, detail 0.970 and boil 0.157 (third lowest in the sweep). But at native resolution the finer claim is right: the blocks stop sharing one grid. Block sizes vary across the frame, edges drift off alignment, and by the middle of the clip the face carries visibly finer stepping than the background. So the mechanism the card identified is real and the timescale is wrong by roughly an order of magnitude - it stays pixel art, it stops being one grid.
pixel_art.works_for: video - SPLIT, and the old 'shimmers apart within a second' prediction is wrong by about an order of magnitude. Over 8.04s the pixel-art LOOK survives clearly at viewing scale (detail 0.970, boil 0.157, third lowest in the sweep) - chunky quantised blocks, aliased stair-stepping and the limited palette all hold. What degrades is grid COHERENCE at native resolution: block sizes drift apart, edges leave alignment, and the face develops finer stepping than the background. Usable for video if the grid is not the point; if it is, the existing advice still applies - run the LTX pass first and quantise per frame afterwards, the way looks/ grades are applied after.
